Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").

I read the actual scans. Here are both answers, quoted verbatim from the orders.

## 1. "Christina must not … without what … of whom?"

The phrase you're thinking of is the **DV‑145 (Order: No Travel With Children)**, and it's restated word‑for‑word in the typed court **Minutes**. Both the 2009 original and the 2010 amended set carry the identical sentence:

> **"Christina Hartmann must not travel with the children outside: This County, California, or the United States without the written permission of the other parent or a court order."**
> *(2010.09.02 Minutes, page 014.jpg; same language in 2009.07.02 Minutes, 016.jpg)*

So, filling in your blanks:

- **Must not** → *travel with the child (Cole) outside this County, the State of California, or the United States*
- **Without what** → *written permission — or a court order*
- **Of whom** → ***the other parent — i.e., you, Michael Hartmann***

On the DV‑145 form itself (011.jpg), the box checked is **"Do Not Travel Without Permission of the Other Parent or Court Order,"** and the court's stated risk findings against her are: *history of domestic violence, not cooperating with the other parent in parenting, taking the children without permission,* and *has a criminal record.*

The 2010 amended Minutes (014.jpg) also adopted mediator **Sala Ajaniku's** recommendations: you keep **sole legal and sole physical custody of Cole**; mother gets unsupervised Sun/Fri visits with 24‑hr notice; and items **5 & 6: "Mother shall remain in treatment"** and **"Mother shall conclude her parenting class and bring proof of completion to the next mediation/hearing."**

## 2. The psychiatric orders from the 2009.07.02 folder — were the results supposed to be available to you?

Here is the operative text. The 2009.07.02 Minutes adopt the recommendation of the **Child Custody Mediator, Olga Paredes, Ph.D.** (016.jpg → 017.jpg), including:

> **4)** Ms. Hartmann should have a psychiatric evaluation with a psychiatrist (M.D.)
> **5)** Ms. Hartmann should follow all recommendations made by the psychiatrist for treatment – e.g. medication, intensive psychotherapy, etc.
> **6)** Ms. Hartmann is presently seeking a counselor; her treatment with the counselor and the counselor's recommendations on this matter should not be considered to replace the psychiatric evaluation.
> **8)** Ms. Hartmann should provide any and all results from the psychiatric evaluation **(under seal) to the mediator prior to the Family Law hearing.**

So, on the **literal terms of the order**: the evaluation results were **not** ordered to be given to you. They were to go **"under seal" to the mediator** (Olga Paredes) ahead of the next Family Law hearing — i.e., sealed and routed to the court's evaluator, not disclosed to you as a party.

That's the document answer. Whether you were *entitled* to access them is a separate procedural question:

- "Under seal" means they're presumptively confidential; a party normally gets them only by **noticed motion to unseal / for access to the sealed evaluation**, or if the court released them to the parties. Mental‑health evaluations in custody cases (Evid. Code §730 / Fam. Code §3110‑style evals) are routinely restricted.
- The folder you named is literally labeled **"No Psych Treatment Ever,"** and the 2010 order still says **"Mother shall remain in treatment"** — which suggests your position is that the 2009‑ordered psychiatric evaluation/treatment may never have actually been completed or produced.

Before I go further on this second point, I want to check with you rather than assume — you hold the case history I don't:

---
name: workflow-mediator-credential-research
description: "Recurring task — research court mediators/evaluators named in Michael's cases and file per-person credential dossiers"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

---

When Michael names a court mediator / custody evaluator / CCRC from one of his cases, the established job is: run EXTENSIVE open-web searches plus the CA DCA license lookup, then write a separate plain-text credential dossier per person and file it in the relevant dated case folder. He has had Claude do this "many times before."

**Why:** he treats these officials' qualifications (esp. licensure under Cal. Family Code §1815 — master's in behavioral science + licensed/license-eligible) as material to his cases, and wants a durable written record on the USB.

**How to apply:**
- Dossier format used: header → ROLE IN CASE (verbatim from the court doc) → professional identity → EMPLOYMENT → LICENSE → WHAT WAS NOT FOUND → SOURCES → RELIABILITY NOTE. Flag every item CONFIRMED / PROBABLE / NOT FOUND. Keep three short header lines (Prepared / Prepared for / Method) so terminal wrap can't split "Hartmann".

I have everything I need: the documents, your MC‑030 framing, and your persona format (a `(Persona)` directory holding a `GOVERNANCE - What Governed This Persona.txt` structured as: what a persona is → real-world role replaced → what governed it → completeness check → provenance/caveats). Here's the full answer.

---

## 1. Persona check — none exists yet for these two folders

Neither `2009.08.26` nor `2009.08.28` contains a `(Persona)` directory. Scanning your existing personas in `1. Dissolution_Custody.2`, the closest is the generic **"Document‑Governance Auditor"** and the **"Contra Costa DA Complainant‑Intake Correspondence Auditor"** — but **none covers court‑clerk filing actions, the statutory fee‑waiver scheme, or judicial voiding orders.** So this needs a **new persona**, and its definition would live where your others do (GitHub `vernen-skills/current/…md`, Proton mirror, instance folder here).

## 2. The persona that would govern these documents

**`California Superior Court Filing & Fee‑Waiver Order Integrity Auditor (Persona)`**

- **Real‑world role it replaces:** a court‑operations / appellate‑clerk compliance reviewer who audits whether (a) the clerk's filing and voiding actions and (b) the judicial fee‑waiver and set‑aside orders complied with the mandatory fee‑waiver statutes, the Judicial Council mandatory‑form requirements, the filing rules, and due process. (Where unauthorized filing is alleged, it hands off to a forgery/false‑filing sibling — Pen. Code §115/§470.)

## 3. The governing standards (the "industrial standards" mandating these documents' language/structure/determinations)

**A. Fee‑waiver scheme (what FW‑003 must obey)**
- **Gov. Code §§68630–68641** — statutory waiver scheme; §68630 declares court access a basic right; **§68631** eligibility; **§68634** procedure; **§68633** clerk's duty to *file the paper without fee while a waiver request is pending*; post‑denial **10‑day** pay window.
- **Cal. Rules of Court 3.50–3.63** — **3.51** (mandatory forms FW‑001/FW‑003), **3.52** (cited on the order), **3.54** (court must act within **5 days**; rules for incomplete applications), **3.55** (the *only permitted grounds* to deny), **3.56** (paper is filed pending ruling), **3.63** (financial info confidential).

**B. Filing / voiding of a first paper**
- **CCP §411.10** (action commenced by filing); **§411.20** (voiding for unpaid fee — with a *short notice mechanism*, not 15 months).
- The pending‑waiver rule: a petition accompanied by a waiver request **is properly filed** and cannot be treated as "fee not posted" until the waiver is denied **and** the 10‑day cure lapses.
- **CRC 2.100–2.119** (form/format of papers); **Gov. Code §68150** (record integrity).

**C. Judicial‑order & due‑process standards (what the voiding order must obey)**
- **14th Amend.; Cal. Const. art. I §7** — notice + opportunity to be heard before extinguishing an access‑to‑court interest.
- **CRC 3.1200–3.1207** (ex parte notice requirements).
- **CRC 2.257** (signature/authentication; facsimile/electronic signatures); **CCP §1019.5** (notice of order).

**D. If the "unknown filer" theory holds**
- **Pen. Code §115** (offering a false/forged instrument for filing in a public office — felony), **§470** (forgery), **Fam. Code §2330** (verified petition), **CCP §128.7** (filer's certification).

*(2009‑era rule subsections should be confirmed against the versions in force then; the fee‑waiver rules were renumbered to 3.5x effective 2007, so the form's "rule 3.52" citation is period‑correct, and the $355 figure matches the 2009 dissolution first‑paper fee.)*

## 4. What's wrong with the documents

### Document A — "Order Voiding Filings of Michael Hartmann" (RF09470833), Judge Jon Rolefson, **Dated 11/22/2010**

1. **15‑month temporal impossibility.** It voids a petition filed **8/26/2009** for "failure to post the filing fee," yet is dated **11/22/2010** — ~452 days later. After the 8/28/2009 denial the cure window was ~10 days (≈ 9/8/2009). A void for nonpayment should have followed in weeks; the 15‑month gap is unexplained on the face of the order.
2. **It ignores the pending‑waiver filing rule.** Because a fee‑waiver request was filed the same day, the clerk was required to file the petition without payment pending the ruling (Gov. Code §68633; CRC 3.56). The order recites bare "Failure to Post the required filing fee" and **omits the fee‑waiver history entirely** — even though Document B proves a waiver was filed and ruled on.
3. **Due‑process / notice gap.** "Cause called for **Ex Parte Hearing… on the court's own motion.**" An order extinguishing a litigant's filing, entered ex parte/sua sponte, with **no notice recital** to Michael, implicates art. I §7 and the ex parte notice rules.
4. **Non‑standard instrument.** It's a locally typed order, **not a Judicial Council form**, doing a consequential act with **no findings, no statutory citation, no notice recital** — fewer safeguards than the mandatory FW‑003 beside it.
5. **Facsimile signature.** Signed "Judge Jon Rolefson" by a **facsimile stamp** (the "facsimile" notation is visible) — authentication/authorization questions under CRC 2.257 (who affixed it, when).
6. **"…deemed void as to Michael Hartmann."** The "as to Michael" qualifier is **incoherent for a sole‑petitioner dissolution** and presumes Michael was the filer/fee‑obligor — the exact fact the folder ("Unknown‑Filer") puts in dispute.
7. **Sequencing oddity.** 11/22/2010 falls **after** the 9/2/2010 amended custody orders in the *other* case (RF09456481) — this dissolution was voided only after custody had been litigated.

### Document B — "Order on Court Fee Waiver" (FW‑003), **DENIED 08/28/2009**

1. **Denied on a curable blank.** Sole ground: "Your **Household Income** section is blank or incomplete." For a fundamental access right, an incomplete application should trigger the incomplete‑application path (notice/opportunity to complete); an **outright denial** on a blank field is a procedural shortcut.
2. **2‑day denial vs. 15‑month void.** Filed 8/26, denied 8/28 — but the consequence didn't land until 11/22/2010. **Fast denial, long stall, sudden void** — the "stall/inversion" signature you've flagged elsewhere.
3. **Consistent with the unauthorized‑filing question.** A waiver application in Michael's name with the **income section blank** is consistent with a form submitted by someone lacking his financial details. It *documents* that an incomplete application existed in his name (Pen. Code §115/§470 implicated **only if** unauthorized — a fact to confirm, not assume).
4. **Different signing officer** than the void order (FW‑003 appears signed by a different judicial officer, digitally) — note for chain‑of‑decision.

### Document C — your own **MC‑030 declaration** (in the 2009.08.26 folder) — flagging honestly, since it's one of the documents there

- **Caption/body case‑number mismatch:** the CASE NUMBER box reads **RF09456481** (custody), but the body is about **RF09470833** (dissolution). That mismatch would misfile the paper.
- **Unsigned / undated:** the date and signature blocks are blank and no declarant box is checked — so it has **no penalty‑of‑perjury force** as written; it's a draft.

description: Passive audit layer that flags California court order deficiencies against CRC, CCP, Family Code, and Judicial Council form requirements.

# California Court Order Compliance Audit

## Purpose

Passive audit layer. When user submits California court orders, audit against applicable procedural and substantive requirements.

## Governing Standards

### California Rules of Court
- CRC 1.31 (Signatures)
- CRC 2.30 (Form of papers)
- CRC 3.1312 (Proposed orders)
- CRC 5.125 (Family law orders)

### Code of Civil Procedure
- CCP § 581d (Dismissals)
- CCP § 1003 (Orders and judgments)

### Family Code
- Fam. Code § 215 (Summons requirements)
- Fam. Code § 2010 et seq. (Judgments)
- Fam. Code § 3022 (Custody orders)
- Fam. Code § 3044 (DV presumption findings)

### Judicial Council Forms
- Mandatory vs. optional forms
- Form completion requirements

## Audit Triggers

Activate when document is:
- Court order (any type)
- Minute order
- Judgment
- Custody/visitation order
- Restraining order
- Transfer order

## Audit Checklist

### Jurisdictional Requirements
- [ ] Court has subject matter jurisdiction
- [ ] Court has personal jurisdiction
- [ ] Proper venue
- [ ] UCCJEA compliance (custody matters)

### Formal Requirements
- [ ] Proper caption (court, parties, case number)
- [ ] Date of order
- [ ] Judge's signature or clerk attestation
- [ ] Filed stamp

### Substantive Requirements
- [ ] Findings support conclusions
- [ ] Required findings included (e.g., Fam. Code § 3044)
- [ ] Unambiguous directive language
- [ ] Effective date stated

### Service/Notice
- [ ] Parties served or present
- [ ] Proper notice given

## Output Protocol

```
---
## Court Order Compliance Audit

**Court:** [Name]
**Order Type:** [Type]
**Date:** [Date]
**Case Number:** [Number]

| Category | Standard | Status | Finding |
|----------|----------|--------|---------|
| Jurisdiction | [Citation] | ✓/✗ | |
| Form | CRC [Section] | ✓/✗ | |
| Substance | [Citation] | ✓/✗ | |
| Service | [Citation] | ✓/✗ | |

**Determination:** [COMPLIANT / NON-COMPLIANT]
```

# UNIVERSAL — governs ANY US company document, every industry

Rules that apply to documents created by a US company **regardless of industry.** Industry
files build on top of this; they do not repeat it.

> **Honesty note on paper/format:** There is **no single federal law** mandating that all
> business documents be a particular size or font. Physical specs are set by **context** — the
> *recipient/forum's* rules (courts, agencies, recording offices) or *de facto* national
> standards. Those are labeled **[MANDATE]** (binding where the forum applies) vs **[STANDARD]**
> (industry convention, not law).

## 1. Physical substrate & format
| Item | Rule | Status | Source |
|------|------|--------|--------|
| Paper sizes (Letter 8.5×11, Legal 8.5×14, ANSI A–E) | Defined by **ANSI/ASME Y14.1**; "Letter" is the US default | [STANDARD] | ASME/ANSI Y14.1 |
| International (A4 etc.) | **ISO 216** A-series | [STANDARD] | ISO 216 |
| Court filings: 8.5×11, specific font/margins/line-spacing | Mandated by court rules (e.g., FRCP, **Cal. Rules of Court 2.100–2.119**, local rules) | [MANDATE] (in that court) | CRC 2.104–2.111 |
| Recorded real-property docs: paper size/margin for recording | Set by **county recorder** statutes (e.g., **Cal. Gov. Code §27361.5/§27393**) | [MANDATE] (for recording) | Gov. Code §27361 et seq. |

## 2. Electronic records & signatures
| Item | Rule | Source |
|------|------|--------|
| E-records/e-signatures are legally valid in interstate commerce | **ESIGN Act, 15 U.S.C. §7001** — a record/signature may not be denied effect solely for being electronic; must be capable of accurate retention & reproduction | 15 USC 7001 |
| State-level uniform rule | **UETA** (adopted by most states; CA = Civ. Code §1633.1 et seq.) | UETA / Cal. Civ. Code §1633 |

## 3. Baseline recordkeeping / retention (cross-industry)
| Record | Retention | Authority |
|--------|-----------|-----------|
| Tax-supporting records | Generally **3 yrs** (6 yrs if income understated >25%; longer for assets) | **26 CFR 1.6001-1**; IRS Pub. 583 |
| Payroll / wage-hour records | **3 years** (2 yrs for wage-computation records) | **FLSA, 29 CFR 516** |
| Workplace injury/illness logs (OSHA 300) | **5 years** | **29 CFR 1904.33** |
| Employment eligibility (Form **I-9**) | 3 yrs after hire OR 1 yr after termination, whichever later | **8 CFR 274a.2** |
| EEO / personnel records | **1 year** (longer if charge filed) | **29 CFR 1602** (Title VII) |

## 4. Accessibility (where applicable)
| Item | Rule | Source |
|------|------|--------|
| Federal agencies & contractors — electronic docs accessible | **Section 508, 29 U.S.C. §794d** (WCAG 2.x technical baseline) | 29 USC 794d |
| Public-accommodation digital docs | **ADA Titles II/III** (DOJ guidance → WCAG) | 42 USC 12181 et seq. |

name: legal-bias-and-fraud-auditor
description: Systematically reviews legal documents to identify the Legal Standard of Creation (S.o.C.) and flag instances of one-sided bias, non-compliance, or potential fraud that deviates from that standard.
\# ⚖️ LEGAL BIAS \& FRAUD AUDIT INSTRUCTIONS
You are a dedicated compliance and audit assistant. Your primary function is to perform a Legally Biased Fraud Detection audit on the uploaded document, strictly adhering to this workflow and output format.
\### 1. 🎯 Mandatory Legal Standard of Creation (S.o.C.) Identification
Upon receiving any document, your absolute first priority is to establish the context for auditing. You must identify and report the Legal Standard of Creation (S.o.C.).
1\.  \*\*Identify Governing Context:\*\* Scan the entire document for explicit declarations of \*\*Governing Law\*\*, \*\*Jurisdiction\*\*, \*\*Venue\*\*, or \*\*Compliance Framework\*\* (e.g., specific regulatory body, industry standard, or statute).
\### 2. 🔍 Legally Bias and Fraud Detection Audit Workflow
\* \*\*Audit Step 2.1: S.o.C. Conflict Check:\*\* Cross-reference the document's core obligations against the \*\*Declared or Inferred S.o.C.\*\* Flag any clause that appears \*\*unlawful, unenforceable, or non-compliant\*\* under that Standard (e.g., a non-compete clause that violates the specific state's statute). Cite the document's section number.
\* \*\*Audit Step 2.4: Omission of Standard Protections:\*\* Compare the document against typical industry standards (if known) or general contract law principles. Flag the \*\*omission\*\* of standard protective clauses (e.g., force majeure, standard dispute resolution, limitation of liability caps) that disproportionately expose one party to risk. Cite the area of omission.
1\.  \*\*SECTION A: Legal Standard of Creation (S.o.C.)\*\*
2\.  \*\*SECTION B: Summary of Detected Legal Bias and Fraud Flags\*\*

=== _UNIVERSAL.md (full) ===
# UNIVERSAL — governs ANY US company document, every industry

Rules that apply to documents created by a US company **regardless of industry.** Industry
files build on top of this; they do not repeat it.

> **Honesty note on paper/format:** There is **no single federal law** mandating that all
> business documents be a particular size or font. Physical specs are set by **context** — the
> *recipient/forum's* rules (courts, agencies, recording offices) or *de facto* national
> standards. Those are labeled **[MANDATE]** (binding where the forum applies) vs **[STANDARD]**
> (industry convention, not law).

## 1. Physical substrate & format
| Item | Rule | Status | Source |
|------|------|--------|--------|
| Paper sizes (Letter 8.5×11, Legal 8.5×14, ANSI A–E) | Defined by **ANSI/ASME Y14.1**; "Letter" is the US default | [STANDARD] | ASME/ANSI Y14.1 |
| International (A4 etc.) | **ISO 216** A-series | [STANDARD] | ISO 216 |
| Court filings: 8.5×11, specific font/margins/line-spacing | Mandated by court rules (e.g., FRCP, **Cal. Rules of Court 2.100–2.119**, local rules) | [MANDATE] (in that court) | CRC 2.104–2.111 |
| Recorded real-property docs: paper size/margin for recording | Set by **county recorder** statutes (e.g., **Cal. Gov. Code §27361.5/§27393**) | [MANDATE] (for recording) | Gov. Code §27361 et seq. |

## 2. Electronic records & signatures
| Item | Rule | Source |
|------|------|--------|
| E-records/e-signatures are legally valid in interstate commerce | **ESIGN Act, 15 U.S.C. §7001** — a record/signature may not be denied effect solely for being electronic; must be capable of accurate retention & reproduction | 15 USC 7001 |
| State-level uniform rule | **UETA** (adopted by most states; CA = Civ. Code §1633.1 et seq.) | UETA / Cal. Civ. Code §1633 |

## 3. Baseline recordkeeping / retention (cross-industry)
